liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lazy Lightning** (2 reviews): Long, jammed-out Lazy Lightning into Supplication is what makes the first set special; Peggy-O and Bird Song also stand out; Lazy Lightning>Supplication and Help>Slip>Franklin's both called mind-blowing, with Garcia blazing [17][20]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Franklin's takes off around halfway and jams hypnotically, with Garcia playing blistering leads toward the climax; Help>Slip>Franklin's is epic, especially Franklin's [25][27]
- **Space** (2 reviews): Space turns very odd, then becomes a lovely duet between Weir and Garcia leading into Uncle John's Band; Mickey's Space featured Tibetan bells; Uncle John's Band also praised [16][21]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Garcia's work on Peggy-O is noteworthy; Lazy Lightning and Supplication are enjoyable [23]
- **Help On the Way** (1 review): Help>Slip>Franklin's is fast, loud and blazing, with Garcia's guitar outstanding [19]
- **Slipknot!** (1 review): Slipknot! is excellent, and Lazy Lightning>Supplication very good; Might As Well and Uncle John's Band are nice [26]
- **Playing in the Band** (1 review): Playin' here is delicate and forceful; near the end a new-age jam includes Weir's seagull noises [24]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer's personal favorite Uncle John's Band, described as shining like a sunrise [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Wavy Gravy**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-09-06.beyerm201.holbrook.35084.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 166 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1983-09-06.111711.Sennheiser421.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 170 min; rated 2.5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1983-09-06.mtx.seamons.95820.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 173 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1983-09-06.147910.mtx.photoleon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 172 min [4]. Said about its sound: Drums is audience-only mix from 3:21 on; Not Fade Away ending uses three sources [4]
- **gd1983-09-06.170742.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 173 min [6]
- **gd83-09-06.sbd.clugston.5489.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 159 min; rated 4.17/5 by 41 [11]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound is excellent and conveys the band interplay beautifully; Sound quality is excellent, though the audience patches are regrettable; Sound is odd with level/EQ issues until Hell In A Bucket, plus some splices; audience patches are seamless [17][20][26][27]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Garcia was deep in a drug fog but his playing skills were not yet eroded [19]
- Three police helicopters searching for rock climbers circled overhead, their searchlights sweeping the Rocks during the show [21]
- Peggy-O and Minglewood got the crowd rocking; reviewer says the band rarely plays anything mediocre at Red Rocks [27]
- Second set has less raw energy than early-summer shows like Sunday's Greek and SPAC, but strong band interplay [17]
- Reviewer considers it one of the best shows of the year [20]
- Second set from Help on the Way through Brokedown Palace is among the Dead's finest music, far better than first set [23]
- Reviewer sees 1980s Playin' as a link to 1970s Dark Stars and calls this possibly the best early-'80s pre-drums segment [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-09-06.beyerm201.holbrook.35084.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Executive Crew (T.P. K.H.); transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Beyer M201's (X-Y) > Sony TCD5M (Maxell MX 90, no dolby) 140 feet from stage (behind board) [1]
- **gd1983-09-06.111711.Sennheiser421.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: source: 2 Sennheiser 421 microphones > Sony TC-D5M - master analog cassettes; [2]
- **gd1983-09-06.mtx.seamons.95820.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [3]. Also: Matrix: soundboard cassette master transferred via cassette and DAT to CDR, patched and mastered by Scott Clugston; Audience portion recorded with Beyer M201 mics into Sony TCD5M, 140 feet from stage behind the board; Patched from 5:06 of Not Fade Away; released to circulation via etree by Tim Burke on June 13, 2006 [3]
- **gd1983-09-06.147910.mtx.photoleon.t-flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Joe Noel; source: A photoLeon Matrix [4]. Also: Matrix mix by Joe Noel using Audacity; rough for first few minutes of set one, then settles; Nine-plus minutes missing from Space on the soundboard were patched with a two-source audience mix [4]
- **gd1983-09-06.170742.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Wiseman, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [6]
- **gd83-09-06.sbd.clugston.5489.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT > CDR, with AUD patches from 2 Master Audience Cassettes: Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5, Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony… [11]. Also: Besides Not Fade Away, an audience patch also appears near the end of Bird Song [26]
